turn1.explanation: The unit responds to two unrelated things: close-up cat faces (eyes, nose, whiskers) and car bodywork (hoods, grilles, glossy painted panels, often of vintage cars).
turn1.evidence: Cat faces make up most of the strongest activations (#1, 2, 4–9), and cars fill most of the rest (#3, 10–15, 17–19) at similar levels. The car crops include side and rear views with no face-like front (#12, #17, #18), so a 'face' reading does not unify them.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on other animal faces (dogs, other felines) and on non-car glossy or chrome objects, which would show whether a shared visual feature links the two groups.
